name: Ed Markey
role: U.S. senator from Massachusetts (2013–present); U.S. representative (1976–2013)
summary: Ed Markey is a progressive Democrat who authored the Green New Deal resolution in the Senate and has made climate, telecommunications and consumer privacy his signature issues. He backs Medicare for all, abortion rights, gun control, same-sex marriage and nuclear arms control, and opposes fossil fuel expansion and Social Security privatization.

abortion-legal.rationale: Called the Dobbs ruling the tearing down of nearly 50 years of protections and the overbroad state abortion bans extremist; urged passing the Women's Health Protection Act to restore Roe.

arms-reduction.rationale: Opposed the $1 trillion defense budget and the Golden Dome missile shield as triggering a nuclear arms race, and urged arms control; no minimum level stated.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted Yea on ratifying the 2022 protocols admitting Finland and Sweden to NATO.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Senate author of the Green New Deal resolution; defended it on the floor and called for phasing out fossil fuels.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called for phasing out fossil fuels and building clean economies in his 2023 COP28 remarks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Describes himself as Senate author of the Transgender Bill of Rights and told the Senate that every transgender person deserves to live without discrimination.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Backed a 2026 Senate resolution recognising sea-level rise due to human-caused climate change and blamed decades of fossil fuel pollution.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Attacked Republican plans to privatize Social Security and hand benefits over to Wall Street.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Argued in 2014 that after Citizens United and McCutcheon unlimited, undisclosed campaign money is corrupting democracy and that he would act to repair it.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for the 1993 Brady Act (1993) and the 1994 assault weapons ban in House roll calls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said the FCC was not created to punish networks for opinions or to be the speech police, opposing government pressure on broadcasters.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Said in 2015 that millions of American workers cannot make ends meet on the minimum wage and backed a budget amendment for that reason; no figure for a living wage stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Told the Senate in 2014 that we must clearly acknowledge past genocides, naming the Armenian genocide, and commemorated it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Urged protection of Dreamers from deportation in a 2018 speech; no restriction measure of his own found.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Criticised a nominee for opposing regulation of environment, worker treatment and consumer safety "in almost any form", defending those rules.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted Nay on the 1996 Defense of Marriage Act and Yea on the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act, which repealed it and required recognition of same-sex marriages.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Listed forgiving the loans of nearly 4 million students among the uses of the money Golden Dome would cost; no specific amount stated as policy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Denounced tax cuts and tax breaks for billionaires paid for by cutting health care, and said wealthy polluters and ultrawealthy individuals should pay; no specific rate stated.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Voted Yea on the 2015 Senate amendment to reaffirm the prohibition on torture (78-21).

unions-good.rationale: Described four decades of fighting and organizing alongside unions and workers, and framed repeal of pension offsets as justice for public servants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Told a 2024 Senate hearing that the country needs a health care system for everyone, supported by Medicare for all, and recalled fighting for a single-payer system in 2009.

notes: Searched his Voteview roll calls (House 1976-2013, Senate 2013-present) and his Congressional Record floor speeches and hearing turns (2013-2026) by theme: health care, wages, tax, unions, guns, abortion, marriage, immigration, climate and energy, nuclear arms, war powers, NATO, Israel and Iran, torture, surveillance, courts, voting and the filibuster, trade, campaign finance, church and state, the UN and the ICC. Votes that fit either reading of a statement (Patriot Act and FISA, Iraq 2002, Keystone, border amendments) were left null. His books and Miller Center texts: none exist for him. Record on most economy, government and world statements is silent or ambiguous, so the uncertainty rule fails.
